hypothesis: The price anchor helps once isolated from the EV floor it was previously confounded with
change: logit(p)=logit(p_price)+w*(logit(p_model)-logit(p_price)) applied to the whole ensemble; every grid cell built twice, anchor off and on
metric: held-out SELECT-B units at matched (spec, EV floor, collapse)
acceptanceCriterion: (1) pooled units improve at EV floor 0.00; (2) >=6 of 11 markets improve; (3) strong markets keep >=11/12 splits in profit
result: units on 33399.6 vs off 36685.0; 4 of 11 markets improved; strong-market cells in profit 917/984 vs 945/984
why: All three conditions failed. The earlier confound is removed and the answer is unchanged, so the anchor is closed permanently. Per-market detail shows it helps only pitcher_outs stably (+1730 to +2190 units at every EV floor, 78-85% of cells) and hurts batter_hits/batter_total_bases/spreads consistently.

hypothesis: Predicted EV is miscalibrated; a chronologically fitted edge->profit map improves board selection
change: isotonic map from predicted EV to realised profit, fitted only on earlier walk-forward folds, applied to the EV FILTER only (side and confidence untouched)
acceptanceCriterion: units improve and strong markets keep 11/12 splits in profit
result: units on 24277.7 vs off 34062.4; 2 of 8 markets improved; strong-market cells in profit 835/984 vs 945/984
why: Failed its criterion. It DOES lift held-out ROI on 6 of 8 markets (pitcher_strikeouts -1.46->+2.07, pitcher_outs -1.51->+1.47, batter_total_bases 1.44->3.52) but cuts board size 50-75%, so units fall. The measurement it produced is the round's most important number and is carried forward as evidence, not as an adoption.

hypothesis: Measurement only: does a nominal x% edge pay x%?
metric: predicted vs realised edge by bucket
result: pooled: 0-1% bucket predicts 0.49% pays -3.20%; 3-5% predicts 3.96% pays -2.00%; 10%+ predicts 19.61% pays 1.95%
why: Predicted edge is barely related to realised edge and is overstated by 3 to 18 percentage points at every level. The EV filter is close to useless as a ranking signal. This is the winner's curse, and it is a selection problem that a better probability model does not fix.

hypothesis: Choosing selection knobs on a gate-aligned objective (ROI subject to a sample floor) rather than on units converts near-miss markets into passes
change: per market, on SELECT-A only: side, confidence floor in {60,65,70,75,80} (never below 60), EV floor >= the global floor. Tightening only, so every board is a strict subset of the incumbent's
validationPeriod: SELECT-B (held out), scored by the SHIPPED gate
metric: count of (market,cut) splits whose SELECT-B board is a mlbgate PASS
acceptanceCriterion: (1) gate passes exceed the incumbent's; (2) strong markets do not lose gate passes
result: arm B 11 passes, arm C 13, incumbent 13; strong markets arm B 8, arm C 10, incumbent 10
why: Neither arm exceeded the incumbent. Arm C ties on passes and improves median ROI (3.34 vs 2.80) but a tie is not the pre-registered bar. Established independently of the verdict window that totals, spreads, h2h, pitcher_strikeouts, pitcher_outs and batter_home_runs clear the gate on 0 of 3 held-out cuts under EVERY rule tested.

hypothesis: More and more recent data improves the result (entry price pulled at T-1h)
change: 2,106 new events fetched from the Odds API historical endpoint: 2026-06..09 all markets, 2026-03..05 unpriced games, 2025-04/05 for two markets. Graded rows 412,886 -> 535,961; games 3,940 -> 5,397
testPeriod: verdict window read ONCE after the run
acceptanceCriterion: expanded data adopted iff the both-gates PASS count does not fall
result: verdict PASS 2/11 vs 4/11; full-OOS PASS 8/11 vs 9/11
why: Failed. BUT the run is confounded by a defect in the ingest, found afterwards by probe_entry_lead.ts: the warehouse entry snapshot sits ~6.0h before first pitch for 2024-03..2025-10 and ~1.0h for 2026-04/05, while this pull used 1h. A one-hour line is sharper than a six-hour one, so the expanded set mixed two price conventions and the comparison measured that mismatch as well as the extra data. Superseded by E25b.

hypothesis: The same expansion, with the entry price pulled at the warehouse's own T-6h convention
change: identical event set, ENTRY_LEAD_H=6.0 so the new rows match the lead the warehouse itself uses for 395k of the 536k graded rows
testPeriod: verdict window read ONCE after the run
acceptanceCriterion: expanded data adopted iff the both-gates PASS count does not fall, and parity_audit prints 0
result: verdict PASS 5/11 vs 4/11; full-OOS PASS 7/11 vs 9/11; BOTH-GATES PASS 5 vs 4; parity_audit 0 of 21,973 rejected. Gained pitcher_strikeouts, batter_runs_scored, pitcher_outs; lost batter_rbis and batter_total_bases.
why: Met its criterion: the both-gates PASS count rose 4 -> 5 and parity still prints 0. The entry-lead fix alone was worth three markets (T-1h gave 2/11, T-6h gives 5/11), which says the price convention mattered more than the extra rows. Verdict windows also move much later (2025-08..2026-09 rather than 2025-05..2026-05), so the test is now more recent and more production-like. batter_runs_scored gains a genuine 2025-2026 verdict window in place of a 2024-only one.

hypothesis: A side policy that discards most of the board is fitted to a thin slice of SELECT and will not survive out of sample
change: choose_side restricted to sides whose SELECT-A board keeps at least f of the both-sides board, f in {0.25,0.40,0.50}; fall back to "both" if none qualifies. Objective unchanged (SELECT-A units)
validationPeriod: SELECT-B (held out), scored by the SHIPPED gate
metric: count of (market,cut) splits whose SELECT-B board is a mlbgate PASS
acceptanceCriterion: gate passes EXCEED the unguarded arm at every f, and strong markets do not lose passes, at every f
result: gate passes 9 vs 9 at f=0.25, 0.40 and 0.50; strong markets 9 vs 9 at every f. f=0.50 does lift held-out units (245.96 vs 205.01) and median ROI (2.54 vs 0.24) but ties on passes
why: Ties, and the criterion was "exceed". The guard also barely binds inside SELECT-A: the smallest share any arm keeps there is 0.42 (pitcher_outs), so the batter_total_bases collapse to 409 rows happens on the FULL SELECT half and not on the inner cuts the nested test uses. The fragility is therefore reported as a known property of the expanded baseline rather than patched.

hypothesis: One global estimator is not right for eleven markets with different target distributions
change: Per market, choose one ensemble member by log loss: the shipped six plus RandomForest, ExtraTrees and three re-tuned HistGradientBoosting configs (gbmB/C/D). LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost not importable and installing a dependency needs sign-off
metric: log loss (proper scoring rule) on SELECT-B
acceptanceCriterion: same member chosen on SELECT-A at ALL three cuts AND beats the global spec on SELECT-B by >0.0011 at all three
result: 4 of 11 markets qualified: spreads->price (mean gain 0.0143), pitcher_strikeouts->price (0.0055), pitcher_outs->price (0.0020), batter_total_bases->rf (0.0015). totals and batter_runs_scored beat the noise band at all three cuts but switched member between cuts, so were not adopted
why: Three of the four resolve to the PRICE with the model removed entirely, which is an earlier stage's "the model is worse than the price on 9 of 11 markets" arriving through an adoption test. But run as written the rule made things WORSE (both-gates 5 -> 4): a member better calibrated to the price disagrees with it less, and a prop board is exactly the rows where the model disagrees, so price overrides starved the boards (pitcher_strikeouts 2,407 rows -> 1). Amended with a SELECT-only viability condition -- the SELECT board must hold >= 500 rows, the gate's own floor -- which keeps batter_total_bases->rf and spreads->price and rejects the two starving ones. Both-gates 5 -> 6.

hypothesis: An average of two members beats either alone (Phase 13 ensembles)
change: Override candidate set widened from 11 single members to all 1- and 2-member averages (66 candidates). All three E26 guards unchanged
metric: log loss on SELECT-B, then the gate
acceptanceCriterion: both-gates PASS count EXCEEDS the 6/11 the single-member rule produced, parity still 0
result: both-gates 4/11 vs 6/11. Overrides became spreads->price and pitcher_outs->price+gbmC; the batter_total_bases->rf override that repaired that market was displaced
why: Worse, and for the reason E16 predicted: widening a pool without adding information is pure overfit risk. The wider search found pairs that win SELECT-A log loss by a hair and lose the one override that was doing real work.
